Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard global variable definitions and array declarations typical of AUR packages. The top-level scope consists of variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, arch, url, license, provides, depends, options, source, sha256sums) and simple parameter expansions using already-defined variables. No command substitutions, network requests, file downloads, or execution of external programs occur at the global scope. All code that performs network operations (git/github URLs) is only referenced in variable definitions and would not be executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The functions `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` are defined but not executed during this step, so their contents are out of scope for this gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard PKGBUILD with safe top-level variable definitions only.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<details>
This is a standard .SRCINFO metadata file for the `varn` AUR package. It declares the package metadata, dependencies (glibc, libgcc), build options (!lto, !strip), and a single source tarball fetched from the package's own upstream GitHub repository at a pinned tag (v0.3.1). The source URL (`https://github.com/flawme/varn/archive/v0.3.1.tar.gz`) is consistent with the declared upstream (`url = https://github.com/flawme/varn`), and the tarball is pinned with a SHA256 checksum (`b45553e8...`), which is good practice for a non-VCS source. There is no executable content, no obfuscation, no suspicious commands, and no evidence of supply-chain manipulation. The description ("Local state checkpointing and rollback system for AI agents and automated tools") is consistent with the package purpose and does not raise concerns.
</details>

There is no executable code, no shell commands, no network requests beyond the standard nvchecker GitHub API query, no obfuscated content, and no data exfiltration. The configuration is entirely consistent with standard AUR maintainer workflow for tracking upstream releases.
</details>
